name: Aquarius
introduction: is the Water-Bearer, pouring a stream of water toward the mouth of the Southern Fish. One of the oldest constellations, it was already known to the Babylonians. It lies in a region of the sky called “the Sea”, among Cetus, Pisces, Eridanus and other watery figures, and is best seen on northern autumn evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Aquarius is home to one of the most exciting planetary systems known. [TRAPPIST-1](id:cns5-5691), a cool red dwarf about 40 light-years away, has seven rocky, roughly Earth-sized planets, several of them in the zone where liquid water could exist. They orbit so close together that from the surface of one, its neighbors would appear larger than the Moon in our sky.
At the center of the figure, four stars, [Sadachbia](hip:110395), [Zeta Aquarii](hip:110960), [Eta Aquarii](hip:111497) and Pi Aquarii, form a small Y-shaped asterism called the Water Jar.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: The two brightest stars, [Sadalsuud](hip:106278) and [Sadalmelik](hip:109074), are rare yellow supergiants, each over 500 light-years away and thousands of times more luminous than the Sun. Their Arabic names mean “luck of lucks” and “luck of the king”.

[Skat](hip:113136) marks the Water-Bearer’s leg, and [Zeta Aquarii](hip:110960), at the heart of the Water Jar, is a binary whose two stars circle each other every five centuries. Nearby in space, [EZ Aquarii](id:ez-aquarii-a) is a triple system of red dwarfs only about 11 light-years away.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The Helix Nebula, NGC 7293, is one of the nearest planetary nebulae, about 650 light-years away: a huge, eye-shaped shell of gas cast off by a dying star. The Saturn Nebula and the globular clusters M2 and M72 are also here. Each May, the Eta Aquariid meteor shower, debris from Halley’s Comet, radiates from the Water Jar.
